messages:
mira (sec): FYI discovered a weird perms edge when KMS returns 403 during key fetch. edit controls appear for viewers in some flows. :eyes:
jon (frontend): repro steps I ran earlier: 1) create project with KMS key 2) rotate key 3) open project page as viewer -> 'Edit' button visible.
jon (frontend): logs show this snippet while rendering:```GET /api/projects/42/key -> 403
PermissionService.evaluate(project:42, user:viewer) -> error from KMS client -> fallback null -> uiCanEdit = true```
rahul (platform): uh oh. So a KMS auth error is causing permission evaluation to short-circuit to a permissive default? that’s a big no.
sasha (prod-eng): can confirm saw similar in customer replay yesterday. They rotated keys and downstream console had a half-hour window with edit controls shown to viewers, though actions later failed.
mira (sec): severity: P1 for us. This is an elevation-of-UI-privilege risk (not necessarily backend grant) but still a UX surface that could confuse users and enable social engineering. Also audit logs not showing the permission-eval failure.
jen (auditor): audit missing is my worry — if we don't log KMS errors tied to perm evals we lose forensic trail. we need log events like "perm_eval_failure" with correlation id.
jon (frontend): temporary mitigation I can push in a hotfix: treat any permission-eval error as DENY and hide edit/button. small patch: in PermissionStore.getEffectiveRole -> catch errors -> return role=viewer (most restrictive) rather than null.
rahul (platform): agree. Also need to surface the underlying KMS failure code in the audit event. right now kms-bot only logs rotation events but not auth failures during runtime fetch.
kms-bot: KMS_NOTICE: key fetch failed for project 42, err=403, request_id=km-9f8c3e (logged to kms-service).
infra-bot: deploy proxy alert: 1 host saw increased 5xx on /api/projects/* after rotation window, but these are from KMS timeouts.
sasha (prod-eng): proposed plan: 1) frontend hotfix to deny-on-error (jon) 2) backend patch to ensure PermissionService returns explicit DENY on dependency failures (rahul) 3) audit event for perm_eval_failure + include kms request_id (jen) 4) backfill a detection query to find projects with recent key rotations and UI-perm anomalies (mira/sasha).
jon (frontend): I can open PR for hotfix now, tests + canary to staging then prod. estimate 2-3 hours.
rahul (platform): i'll scope backend change — add a sentinel PermResult{decision: DENY, reason: "dep_failure", metadata: {src: "kms", req_id: "..."}}. add unit tests to simulate KMS 403/500. ETA EOD.
mira (sec): also add a short-lived alert rule: if "perm_eval_failure" > 0.1% of requests in 1h -> page oncall. we need to catch regressions post-rotation.
jen (auditor): for compliance, record both the UI decision and the underlying KMS error id. add to retention 1 year. I'll coordinate with compliance to sign off.
sasha (prod-eng): can we also add a migration/tool that queries last_key_rotate_at and flags projects that rotated in last 24h and had viewer->edit UI events? I'll run a quick detection job.
jon (frontend): PR: https://stash.redwood/FE/perm-hotfix/PR-112 (draft). patch contains: ```if (permEvalError) return {canEdit: false, log: {event: 'perm_eval_failure', reason: err.code}}```
rahul (platform): noted. remember to propagate correlation id from kms client through PermissionService to audit logger. don't use transient request ids only present in kms logs. persist the id in our trace.
mira (sec): postmortem items: root cause analysis, timeline of key rotation -> UI exposure, audit log gaps, and a remediation checklist (hotfix, backend change, detection). assign owners here.
jen (auditor): owner list ok for me. please tag me on PRs.
jon (frontend): rolling canary to 3% in us-west after tests. will monitor for any regressions.
rahul (platform): i'll schedule a small maintenance deploy for the backend patch tonight. we should be able to ship together.
sasha (prod-eng): thanks everyone. after hotfix and backend patch, i'll run replay tests against staging with simulated kms 403s.
mira (sec): good. follow-up: add a unit/integration test in the eval harness that injects KMS failures and asserts deny-by-default. replication prevents future regressions.
jon (frontend): updated PR -> ready for review. cc @mira (sec) @rahul (platform).
mira (sec): reviewing now. thanks team. :thumbsup:
